assignments.text:
Thus
she, who for the first moment had known no wish
but that of pushing homeward and hiding her
sudden downfall within her own house where
nobody could intrude upon her, had so triumphantly
explained all that trouble away before she got home,
that she entered the Grange radiant, with no sense
of having a downfall to hide. The casuistry of love
is more skilful than any device of philosophy. She
explained everything to herself.
assignments.summary: Catherine enters her home radiant, having completely explained away the scandal through the logic of love.
assignments.best_quote: The casuistry of love is more skilful than any device of philosophy. She explained everything to herself.

assignments.text:
"Cousin Edward," said Hester, suddenly finding
her voice, "you told me just now that I disliked to
walk alone, that I was poor and had no body-guard.
I said, who would harm me? but you have proved
that it was true, and I a fool. I did want a body-guard,
some one to see that I was not insulted, to
protect me, on a quiet country road, from—from—"
assignments.summary: Hester accuses Edward of proving his own rhetoric—that she does need protection—and indicts him for failing to provide it, instead using her vulnerability against her.

assignments.text:

assignments.text:
Hester woke next morning in an unfamiliar room

that had happened, she could not tell what, that
first sensation before memory awakens which is one
of the most bitter indications of having entered upon
the world of evil. So the guilty pair in Paradise, in
the morning of the world, must have woke out of
their sleep, and felt, before remembrance came, the
sense of ill.
assignments.summary: Hester wakes in an unfamiliar room with a terrible sense that something dreadful has occurred, her mind not yet catching up with memory.
assignments.best_quote: So the guilty pair in Paradise, in the morning of the world, must have woke out of their sleep, and felt, before remembrance came, the sense of ill.

dark curtains stood out like ivory. Some time
afterwards she sighed two or three times heavily,
then there was no sound at all. The fire burned
cheerfully, the lamp shed its steady glow upon

had not been reading much to begin with, and now
all her faculties were awakened. She understood no
reason for it, but she understood  it . Not so Catherine,
however, who took no notice, as so often
happens to the person chiefly concerned.
assignments.summary: After Catherine's complacent remark, a charged silence falls; Hester is jolted from her book and grasps some unspoken tension while Catherine, the subject of concern, remains completely unaware.
assignments.best_quote: She understood no reason for it, but she understood it.

assignments.text:
"Which there is not, thank God," she said heartily. And again there ensued that little pause. Was it
possible she did not observe it? No one echoed the
sentiment, no one even murmured the little nothings
with which a stillness, which has a meaning, is
generally filled up by some benevolent bystander. What did it mean? Hester asked herself. But
Catherine took no notice. All had gone so well with
her. She was not afraid of evil tidings.
assignments.summary: Catherine warmly asserts that work is not needed, but another charged silence falls; no one corroborates her sentiment, and the narrator reveals her dangerous lack of fear or suspicion.
assignments.best_quote: All had gone so well with her. She was not afraid of evil tidings.

assignments.text:
"I beg your pardon, Miss Hester," he cried, "I
was just going to tell something of your mother that
would please you. When I told her we wanted
money, she ran to her desk and got out all she had. It was twenty pounds," said the old clerk with a [Pg 136] 
little laugh; "twenty pounds, when we wanted twice
as many thousands! But what did that matter?
assignments.summary: Mr. Rule tells Hester that when asked for help, her mother gave her entire savings of twenty pounds, though thousands were needed—an act of selfless devotion.
assignments.best_quote: When I told her we wanted money, she ran to her desk and got out all she had. It was twenty pounds.

assignments.text:
Hester's heart gave a bound of mingled pleasure
and pain. Perhaps even she had never done justice
to her simple-hearted mother. She sat bolt upright
in her chair, listening with all her might. Catherine
Vernon seemed to retire from the principal place she
had hitherto held in the conversation, and Hester
came forward in her stead. She looked at the old
clerk steadily.
assignments.summary: Hester, moved by the revelation of her mother's sacrifice, sits upright with keen attention; Catherine withdraws from the center of conversation as Hester steps forward.
assignments.best_quote: Hester's heart gave a bound of mingled pleasure and pain.

assignments.text:
"You speak," she said, "of ladies only. Where
was my father?" holding Rule with her eye, so that
he could not escape.
assignments.summary: Hester demands to know where her father was during the crisis when her mother and cousin helped save the bank.
assignments.best_quote: You speak of ladies only. Where was my father?

assignments.text:
"I don't wish to look again. Is not that enough? I suppose it would make her very unhappy. She
would struggle, she would try to find excuses. Oh,
Captain Morgan, don't press me so! I suppose everything
would turn round and round. There would
seem nothing to stand on, nothing to look up to,
the skies would all whirl and the solid ground.
assignments.summary: Hester struggles to articulate the true emotional impact: everything becomes unstable and vertiginous; she is nearly overcome describing it.
assignments.best_quote: There would seem nothing to stand on, nothing to look up to, the skies would all whirl and the solid ground. It makes my head swim to think of it.

assignments.text:
It would have given Catherine Vernon a sharper
shock still if she had seen into Edward's mind as he
went away from her, bitterly feeling that while other
men could taste the sweetness of freedom and of
love, he was attached to an old woman's apron-strings,
and had to keep her company and do her
pleasure, instead of taking the good of his youth
like the rest.
assignments.summary: Edward experiences acute bitterness at his confinement to Catherine's service, envying other men's freedom to taste love and freedom while he remains bound.
assignments.best_quote: It would have given Catherine Vernon a sharper shock still if she had seen into Edward's mind as he went away from her, bitterly feeling that while other men could taste the sweetness of freedom and of love, he was attached to an old woman's apron-strings, and had to keep her company and do her pleasure, instead of taking the good of his youth like the rest.

assignments.text:
It made him angry, it made
him furious; it made him for the moment too much
a natural man, too sincere and real to be capable of
his usual self-suppression. Harry would have an
equal share with himself of the bank; they were
equal there in power and authority, and in the
profits they drew. Why then was it that Harry
should be his own master and Edward the slave of
an old woman!
assignments.summary: Edward's anguish intensifies as he realizes that despite equal status and wealth in the bank, Harry possesses freedom while Edward remains enslaved to Catherine's emotional demands.
assignments.best_quote: Harry would have an equal share with himself of the bank; they were equal there in power and authority, and in the profits they drew. Why then was it that Harry should be his own master and Edward the slave of an old woman!

assignments.text:
He indemnified
himself by plunging into the midst of the
bundle of papers which he had not chosen to
describe to Catherine. In these papers lay far more
excitement than all Harry's privileges had yet
supplied. A battery of artillery planted in front of [Pg 219] 
this peaceful Grange with all its matches alight
would scarcely have been more full of danger.
assignments.summary: Edward finds psychological compensation for his powerlessness in dangerous financial papers that contain more excitement than Harry's romantic freedom.
assignments.best_quote: He indemnified himself by plunging into the midst of the bundle of papers which he had not chosen to describe to Catherine. In these papers lay far more excitement than all Harry's privileges had yet supplied. A battery of artillery planted in front of this peaceful Grange with all its matches alight would scarcely have been more full of danger.

assignments.text:
There was enough in the packet to tear the house
up by its roots, and send its walls flying in a whirlwind
of ashes and ruin. Edward sat down to
examine it as another man might have flown to
brandy or laudanum. Dreams were in it of sudden
successes, of fortunes achieved in a moment. Castles
in the air more dazzling than ever rose in a fairy
tale.
assignments.summary: The papers promise dazzling fantasies of sudden wealth and independence, to which Edward turns like a man seeking oblivion in drink or drugs.
assignments.best_quote: There was enough in the packet to tear the house up by its roots, and send its walls flying in a whirlwind of ashes and ruin. Edward sat down to examine it as another man might have flown to brandy or laudanum. Dreams were in it of sudden successes, of fortunes achieved in a moment. Castles in the air more dazzling than ever rose in a fairy tale.

assignments.text:
He revenged himself on his bonds, on the
superior happiness of his rival, on Catherine above
all, the unconscious cause of his imprisonment, by
this—Here was enough, all ready and in his hands,
to ruin them all.
assignments.summary: Edward projects his desire for revenge and liberation onto the papers, which offer the power to destroy Catherine and Harry simultaneously.
assignments.best_quote: He revenged himself on his bonds, on the superior happiness of his rival, on Catherine above all, the unconscious cause of his imprisonment, by this—Here was enough, all ready and in his hands, to ruin them all.

assignments.text:
"Oh, Hester, it would be easy, very easy, to cease to
be unfortunate—if you choose, dear. All that part
of our life might fly away like a cloud—if you
choose. We might be done with poverty and dependence
and thinking of what Catherine will say
and what people will think. The White House—might
be yours if you liked, everything might be
yours. You would only have to say the word."
assignments.summary: Mrs. John passionately describes the transformation marriage to Harry would bring: freedom from poverty, dependence, and Catherine's control, and the restoration of the White House.
assignments.best_quote: All that part of our life might fly away like a cloud—if you choose. We might be done with poverty and dependence and thinking of what Catherine will say and what people will think. The White House—might be yours if you liked, everything might be yours.

assignments.text:
She could put back her mother in
the White House she loved, take down the innocent
portrait in white satin, and hang it in the place of
honour once more; throw open finer rooms than
Catherine's for the reception of, oh! so different a
company—society in which no one should be overlooked,
and in which Catherine's gentle rival should
be supreme. She could do all this if she chose. The
thought suddenly bursting upon her made her head
go round.
assignments.summary: Hester envisions reversing her mother's exile from the White House and making herself a rival power centre to Catherine.
assignments.best_quote: She could put back her mother in the White House she loved, take down the innocent portrait in white satin, and hang it in the place of honour once more

assignments.text:
It gave her a sort of pang of amusement when she
concluded upon this—Hester! that proud, troublesome
creature—she who would never give in, who
put on the airs of a princess in the Grange drawing-room,
and declined to go to supper—she with the
spirit of a revolutionary, and the temper of a—demon—(no,
no, this was perhaps too bad—the
temper of a—Vernon, Catherine said to herself with
a laugh)—she to fall to the lot of Harry!
assignments.summary: Catherine finds the idea of Hester marrying Harry absurdly amusing—a paradoxical pairing of the ambitious, spirited girl with the placid, athletic young man.
assignments.best_quote: She to fall to the lot of Harry! This was so strangely funny, so paradoxical, so out of character, that it amused Catherine altogether beyond description, yet gave her a strange blow.
